The core insight of 1885 lies in addressing the dual challenge of sparsity and concept drift—two prevalent issues in real-world deployment environments. The paper introduces a majority-vote ensemble of drift detectors tailored for abrupt and gradual changes, leveraging empirical validation from synthetic and real-world datasets including a Walmart change-risk system. The ensemble design ensures resilience against individual detector failures by combining multiple specialized algorithms, thereby reducing the risk of false positives or missed drifts. This approach is grounded in the principle of ensemble diversity, which enhances robustness by minimizing reliance on any single model’s weaknesses. The imputation strategy addresses missing data through kNN-based methods, validated via RMSE comparisons. Temporal precision metrics such as TPD and drift count correct for common pitfalls in evaluating drift detectors, particularly those caused by repeated alarms or offsetting misses. These metrics provide a clearer picture of detector reliability in practical applications. The methodological framework supports both theoretical rigor and operational utility, making it suitable for integration into systems requiring adaptive monitoring and risk assessment.
